units.title: OP Stack chains with a non-ETH gas token
angles: Arithmetic and control flow. Read the interpreter this network runs at the release its endpoint reports, and any compiler, bytecode rewriting, caching or code analysis stage in front of it. Cover the 256 bit integer library and its pinned version, MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMP and JUMPI with the jump destination analysis, KECCAK256, MCOPY, memory expansion and CALLDATALOAD. Compare each with the Ethereum specification at the edges that OPCODES.md lists, and read the release notes and fix commits since the versions OPCODES.md records. Then rerun the scripts in research/network-risk/tools/opdiff (battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py, replay.py) for this unit's chain ids, write the outputs into your work directory, and add vectors for anything the reading makes suspicious. Report every result that differs from the specification, every release that changed these paths, how a wrong result would change the pool math in src/libraries (TickMath, BitMath, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap) or the logic that depends on it, and which validators could run a different code path than the public endpoint.

Upcoming forks. Assume every network upgrade scheduled or proposed for the next six months ships. What changes for the PoolManager and for funds already inside it, and what could an ordinary account do the day after?

Task 1 (L-1294, World Chain): in world-chain v2.8.2 locate the instruction table the node uses for block execution (cycle 35 names table 0x52f92a0 and SLOAD 0x1f25060) and follow SLOAD, SSTORE, TLOAD and TSTORE to the account and slot lookups, the slot insert and growth, the journal entry writers, the transient map, checkpoint, the frame commit, checkpoint_revert and JournalEntry::revert. code.title: Ethereum: the storage read cache and the rewritten arithmetic on erigon's main branch under PoolManager reentry
code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 35 added and a list of what is not covered. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-1298 and L-1285, and F-165. erigon's main branch (3.9.0-dev, not released) returns SLOAD results from a two-entry cache kept in the call frame while a state read stamp is unchanged (execution/vm/interpreter.go lines 124-171 and instructions.go lines 859-880 as read on 2026-11-27), and rewrites DIV, EXP and MULMOD with fast paths on an unreleased integer library commit. Cycle 35 ran the arithmetic on 2,190,028 vectors with no mismatch but did not find where the stamp is defined. The PoolManager is reentered by design: a hook called from beforeSwap or beforeModifyLiquidity may call swap, modifyLiquidity or donate on the same pool, and the outer frame then reads slot0, liquidity, tick words and fee growth again (src/PoolManager.sol:146-230, src/libraries/Pool.sol, src/libraries/Hooks.sol). Both frames run the same contract. A cache that handed the outer frame a slot0 read from before the nested write would compute amounts from a stale price, and the difference would be paid from the single PoolManager balance. Any account can build that shape with a hook on its own pool of real tokens. Erigon is a minority execution client on Ethereum and is also used as a base by other networks' nodes; the actor for a fault here is an operator who runs the future release, and a wrong state root would be rejected by the other clients, so say exactly what an account could and could not gain. Comparing erigon revisions is allowed. Scripts: research/network-risk/cycles/035/ethereum-reference.work (scripts erigon_fastpaths.py, fullmath_div.py, slowalt.py; build/herigon if present). go 1.24 is installed; if erigon main needs a newer toolchain, do not download one: transcribe the cache and the state object methods it depends on into Python or Go that builds here, line for line, and say so. Task 1: fetch execution/vm (interpreter.go, instructions.go, the frame and contract types) and the IntraBlockState sources of erigon main, record the commit, and find the definition of the stamp the cache compares (ReadStamp or whatever the code calls it today). List every place that changes it: SetState, revert to snapshot, SELFDESTRUCT, account creation, a write by another frame of the same address, a write by a DELEGATECALL frame running other code on the same storage, transient storage, and the block-level parallel executor if one touches it. List every place that should change it and does not. Task 2 (L-1298): build a model of the cache with the state object behind it and run these sequences, each compared with a model without the cache: (a) outer frame reads slot S, nested frame of the same contract writes S and returns, outer reads S; (b) the same with the nested frame reverting after the write; (c) nested write, then a deeper frame reverts only itself; (d) the write made through DELEGATECALL into other code; (e) two slots alternating so both cache entries are in use, then a third evicts one; (f) S written back to its original value; (g) a read of S in a STATICCALL frame after the write; (h) the cache of a frame that is entered again at the same depth after its sibling returned (frame object reuse from a pool). Then drive the same shapes with the PoolManager's runtime through tools/opdiff/pyevm.py patched with the cache model: a hook that swaps on the same pool from beforeSwap and from beforeModifyLiquidity, a hook that donates, and a callback that reenters unlock-free functions; compare every returned amount and written slot with unpatched pyevm.py. Task 3: if an erigon endpoint that reports a main or 3.9.0 build can be found among public endpoints (web3_clientVersion), send the reentry shapes of Task 2 by eth_call with state overrides and compare. If none exists, say so; released erigon builds do not carry the cache. Task 4 (L-1285): check whether a 3.9.0 tag or release branch exists, which integer library commit it pins, and whether opDiv, opExp, opMulmod, opCallDataLoad, the PUSH handlers and the cache equal main's. Rerun erigon_fastpaths.py against the tagged code if it exists.
